objective: Find externally demonstrated mechanisms, ablations, reproducible implementations, and failure modes in autonomous-scientist systems that could accelerate O/AGI research without broadening evidence beyond what was tested.

covered_sources.title: Towards end-to-end automation of AI research
A multi-agent system for automating scientific discovery
AutoResearchClaw: Self-Reinforcing Autonomous Research with Human-AI Collaboration
Project2Task: Graph-Guided Project-Level Planning for Autonomous Research
AutoResearchBench: Benchmarking AI Agents on Complex Scientific Literature Discovery
PaperBench: Evaluating AI's Ability to Replicate AI Research
ScienceAgentBench: Toward Rigorous Assessment of Language Agents for Data-Driven Scientific Discovery
MLGym: A New Framework and Benchmark for Advancing AI Research Agents

candidate_mechanisms.description: Template-free AI Scientist uses parallel tree search across four experimental stages (initial investigation, hyperparameter tuning, research-agenda execution, ablations). An evaluator selects the best leaf to seed the next stage. Expansion deliberately sometimes selects buggy nodes for repair; otherwise it uses best-first selection informed by metrics, training dynamics, plots, code critique, and VLM figure critique.
quantitative_evidence: Generated-paper quality increased with newer base-model releases; reported correlation P < 0.00001.
Paper quality increased with additional test-time compute in the reported scaling experiments.
One of three selected workshop submissions received scores 6/7/6 (mean 6.33), above the workshop's average acceptance threshold and in the top 45% of reviewed submissions.
candidate_mechanisms.evidence_scope: Supports the tested AI Scientist configurations and evaluation setup; does not establish that any single tree-search subcomponent alone caused the gains. O's existing checkpoint-inheritance candidate may overlap with stage-to-stage best-leaf inheritance, so that submechanism should not be treated as new without comparison.
candidate_mechanisms.decision_relevance: High for testing parallel branch expansion, explicit error-branch repair, and evaluator-gated stage transitions; medium for checkpoint inheritance because O already evaluated an adapted variant.

candidate_mechanisms.description: Robin separates concise literature search (Crow), deep literature synthesis/verification (Falcon), and data analysis (Finch), then orchestrates them in an almost deterministic workflow rather than relying on free-form agent routing.
quantitative_evidence: Robin analyzed 551 papers in 30 minutes; authors estimate 294 human hours for the same literature work and about a 200-fold time reduction for the whole workflow.

Ablating Falcon, or both Crow and Falcon, caused a dramatic increase in hallucinated references in blinded human reference checks; ablating Crow alone did not, consistent with Falcon correcting/masking upstream citation errors.
candidate_mechanisms.evidence_scope: Citation-quality ablation was tested on Robin's dAMD proposal workflow; the 200-fold total-workflow figure is an author estimate rather than a randomized human comparison.
candidate_mechanisms.decision_relevance: High: suggests a cheap first-pass retrieval plus a separate deep verifier can materially improve grounding, and that deterministic orchestration may be sufficient when tool order is stable.

candidate_mechanisms.description: Represent candidate contributions as innovation atoms in a directed lineage graph, choose horizontal/vertical/hybrid portfolio structure, then emit bounded task contracts with explicit ownership, inputs, artifacts, evaluation requirements, boundaries, dependencies, and execution order; repair overlap and missing fields before execution.
quantitative_evidence: Across 10 project briefs producing roughly 30 tasks, manuscript-based portfolio quality averaged 7.15 versus 4.58 for a brief baseline and 5.31 for a topic-only setting.
Using Project2Task contracts with AutoResearchClaw increased downstream task accuracy from 0.536 to 0.759.
candidate_mechanisms.evidence_scope: Recent preprint; benchmark is small and the reported downstream gain is specific to AutoResearchClaw integration.
candidate_mechanisms.decision_relevance: Very high: directly targets long-horizon research decomposition, overlap avoidance, parallel alternatives, and dependency-aware integration, which are structurally relevant to O's recursive work selection.

candidate_mechanisms.description: AutoResearchClaw couples structured multi-agent debate with a Pivot/Refine self-healing executor, verifiable result reporting, targeted human intervention modes, and cross-run evolution that converts prior failures into future safeguards.
quantitative_evidence: On the reported 25-topic ARC-Bench experiment-stage benchmark, the full system outperformed AI Scientist v2 by 54.7%.
A seven-mode human-in-the-loop ablation found targeted intervention at high-leverage decision points outperformed both full autonomy and exhaustive step-by-step oversight.
candidate_mechanisms.evidence_scope: System-level improvement does not isolate causal contribution of Pivot/Refine, debate, verification, or cross-run evolution individually; only the intervention-policy comparison is explicitly described as an ablation in the abstract.
candidate_mechanisms.decision_relevance: High as a candidate family for failure recovery and selective escalation; requires component-level testing before adoption.

candidate_mechanisms.description: AI co-scientist uses specialized Generation, Reflection, Ranking, Evolution, Proximity, and Meta-review agents with asynchronous worker queues; hypotheses compete in Elo-style tournaments and are evolved under additional test-time compute.
quantitative_evidence: Reported automated hypothesis quality rises with more test-time compute.
Higher internal Elo ratings positively correlate with GPQA Diamond correctness, and small expert studies preferred the system's outputs to baselines.
Several biomedical hypotheses were experimentally validated, including AML drug-repurposing activity and liver-fibrosis targets.
candidate_mechanisms.evidence_scope: Elo is an internal auto-evaluation signal and expert sample sizes were small; laboratory validation supports selected outputs, not the full internal ranking metric as a universally valid objective.
candidate_mechanisms.decision_relevance: Medium-high for asynchronous candidate tournaments and recursive hypothesis evolution; evaluator validity must be independently calibrated.

failure_evidence.observation: On open-ended scientific literature discovery, the best evaluated LLM agents reached only 9.39% accuracy on Deep Research and 9.31% IoU on Wide Research; many strong baselines were below 5%.
failure_evidence.scope: AutoResearchBench's scientific-literature tasks; not a claim that all retrieval systems fail at the same rate.
failure_evidence.implication: Do not equate fluent research summaries with coverage. External research workers should track search recall/coverage evidence and deliberately test deep target-finding and wide collection, not just relevance ranking.

failure_evidence.observation: Best tested agent achieved 21.0% average replication score on 20 ICML 2024 papers; expert humans remained stronger. The automated judge reached F1 0.83 on JudgeEval.
failure_evidence.scope: PaperBench's replication tasks and tested 2025 agent configurations.
failure_evidence.implication: A scientist agent's paper-like output is weak capability evidence unless execution artifacts and granular task-level replication are verified.

failure_evidence.observation: Best evaluated agent solved 32.4% of tasks independently and 34.3% with expert-provided knowledge across 102 real scientific tasks.
failure_evidence.scope: ScienceAgentBench's data-driven scientific coding tasks and tested models/frameworks.
failure_evidence.implication: Expert knowledge alone gave little absolute lift in that setup; implementation/debugging competence remains a distinct bottleneck from context availability.

failure_evidence.observation: Evaluated frontier models generally improved baselines via better hyperparameters but did not generate novel hypotheses, algorithms, architectures, or substantial improvements on MLGym-Bench.
failure_evidence.scope: 13 MLGym-Bench tasks and tested 2025 model configurations.
failure_evidence.implication: Track whether improvements are merely local tuning versus genuinely new mechanism discovery; do not count benchmark gain alone as research novelty.

dead_ends_or_cautions: Do not treat AI Scientist stage-to-stage best-leaf inheritance as novel for O until compared with O's already-tested checkpoint-inheritance candidate.
Do not attribute AutoResearchClaw's 54.7% system-level gain to any one of its five mechanisms without component ablations.
Do not use automated-review scores as sole truth: AI Scientist reports post-cutoff reviewer balanced accuracy of about 66%, and AI co-scientist's Elo is an internal metric.
Do not generalize biological lab-loop success in Robin to computational AI research without matched tests.
next_queries: Find component-level ablations for AutoResearchClaw (Pivot/Refine, debate, verifiable reporting, cross-run evolution) and exact ARC-Bench scoring details.
Inspect Project2Task full paper/code for task-contract ablations, overlap-repair contribution, and whether gains survive different downstream executors.
Extract exact AI Scientist compute-scaling curve and stage/tree-search ablations from supplementary material without re-testing checkpoint inheritance already covered by O.
Search 2026 autonomous-research systems for persistent cross-run memory/evolution with quantitative causal ablations and open traces.
Search scientist-agent verification systems with independently validated in-loop oracles rather than self-judges.
